title: Staged Precision Fallback — Design Sprint Notes
content:
Context:
Sprint / workshop notes from internal SE session (10/03–10/08). Goal: design a lightweight, reproducible approach for customer POCs to gracefully degrade model precision in order to meet latency SLOs while bounding quality regression. This doc captures experiments, config sketches, decision heuristics, and open questions — intended as a practical playbook for pilots (retail + finserv customers).

Goals and success criteria:
- Keep 95th percentile latency below target (configurable per customer) with minimal throughput impact.
- Limit automated precision fallback-induced quality regression: target end-to-end metric drop <= 3% (customer metric like intent F1 / summarization ROUGE-L).
- Fallbacks must be reversible and observable: per-request metadata showing which precision/variant served the response.
- Low friction to test in Dedicated and Hosted environments.

Key constraints remembered from customers:
- Some customers forbid model weight changes in Private deployments — fallback must be runtime-configurable without altering model blobs where possible.
- KV cache coherency (prefix caching) can behave differently with quantized kernels; account for cache invalidation and rewarm cost.
- Regulatory customers prefer deterministic rollbacks and audit logs.

Experiment summary (small benchmark set run during sprint):
- Workload: 3 synthetic traces (chatty Q/A, long-context summarization, short classification).
- Models tested: Llama-2-13b (fp16 baseline), q4_k_mixed-int8 (aggressive), q2/4 hybrid (grouped int4 fallback variant), 7b candidate for scale-down cascade.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), end-task quality (F1 / ROUGE), token-cost estimate, rewarm penalty (ms) when switching cache.

Top-level findings:
1) Progressive precision stepping (fp16 -> int8 mixed -> grouped-int4) provides smoother quality drop vs direct fp16->int4 jump.
2) For chatty workloads with high prefix reuse, falling back to a slightly lower precision while preserving original KV cache (if compatible) reduces apparent quality loss. But kernel incompatibilities force cache invalidation in some combos — add compatibility table in runtime.
3) Thresholds: a safe first-step threshold was observed at p95 latency > 1.15 * target for > 60s sustained; second step triggered at > 1.25 * target. These numbers need customer tuning.
4) Model cascade to a smaller architecture (13b -> 7b) often cost-inefficient unless token-lengths are small; useful as last-resort when under-provisioned for steady traffic.

Config sketches (runtime):
- fallback_policy:
  - precision_steps: ["fp16", "int8_mixed", "grouped_int4"]
  - latency_window_ms: 60000  # measurement window for latency smoothing
  - p95_scale_up_threshold: 1.15
  - p95_escalation_threshold: 1.25
  - cooldown_ms: 300000
  - max_degradation: 2  # number of precision steps allowed

Note: above is prose/config snippet for engineers; exact field names will be mapped to Redwood API fields.

Routing/decision heuristics (sketch):
- Per-route policy that monitors rolling p95 and queue length; if sustained exceeds p95_scale_up_threshold for 60s, attempt next precision step on 10% of traffic (canary).
- If canary OK (no >3% quality drop measured on weighted eval set), rollout to 50% then full rollout with ramp.
- If quality regressions exceed allowed delta or customer alerts, auto-rollback to previous precision and escalate to human.

Observability requirements:
- Annotate responses with: precision_variant, kernel_id, cache_state, route_version, fallback_reason.
- Emit event on every precision change with context: recent p95, queue_depth, sample IDs used for quality checks.
- Integrate with Console for per-model/per-precision dashboards and for fast A/B quality checks using the customer's eval prompts.

KV cache notes and rewarm strategy:
- When kernel/precision incompatible -> drop cache. Rewarm cost measured: 200–1200ms depending on prefix length; for chatty customers this is non-trivial.
- Experiment: maintain a small hybrid cache store that keeps top-N prefixes in fp16 as a fallback to avoid full rewarm when stepping down. Early results: reduces p95 spike by ~25% on rewarm events but increases memory footprint.

Quality-monitoring approach for POC:
- Ship a tiny eval harness: n=50–200 customer-like prompts sampled from live traffic (privacy-safe) or from customer-provided prompt set.
- After canary precision change, run immediate batched eval and compute metric deltas vs baseline. Use simple thresholds to accept/rollback.

Customer-facing UX for POCs:
- Offer 'latency-first' and 'quality-first' presets that pre-populate thresholds and allowed degradation steps.
- Provide a one-click dry-run: simulate 5 minutes of legacy traffic against fallback policy and report expected cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.

Decision log & open questions (from workshop):
- Q1: How to guarantee determinism for compliance-minded Private deployments when using mixed kernels? Action: engineering to document kernel determinism matrix and include explicit audit header. Owner: Marco. ETA: 2025-11-05.
- Q2: Should we persist fallback history to customer-visible audit logs or only to platform ops? Decision lean towards both (customer dashboard + immutable log). Owner: Priya.
- Q3: Can we avoid cache drops when stepping precision by adding on-the-fly conversion layer? Research spike recommended (cost vs latency tradeoffs). Owner: Jonah.

Action items (next sprint):
- Implement a feature-flagged runtime policy prototype (Jonah) — PR track: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/982 (spike branch). Due: 10/31.
- Build 3-route demo template for SE field kits (FP16 baseline + int8 canary + grouped-int4 fallback) and a pre-filled eval prompt set. Owner: Aisha. Due: 10/20.
- Add precision compatibility matrix to Console model detail page and expose 'recommender' warning when a chosen fallback will drop cache. Owner: Lena. Due: 11/12.

Quick experiment log (raw numbers):
- Chat trace: baseline fp16 p95 420ms; int8_mixed p95 360ms (quality delta -0.9%); grouped_int4 p95 310ms (quality delta -2.8%).
- Summarization long-context 1024 tokens: rewarm penalty average 890ms when cache invalidated.
- Cost estimate per 1M tokens: fp16 $X; int8_mixed ~0.65*X; grouped_int4 ~0.45*X (rough).

Customer handoff checklist for POC kickoff:
- Confirm SLOs (p95 target), tolerance for quality regression, and allowable fallback steps.
- Obtain or generate a 100–200 prompt eval set representative of core flows.
- Select default policy preset (latency-first / quality-first) and tune thresholds in initial week.
- Prep monitoring dashboard: p50/p95, precision distribution, sample diffs, cache-rewarm events.

Closing note: staged precision fallbacks look like a pragmatic lever for latency SLOs in the field. The major risk is cache incompatibility and the hidden rewarm cost — both must be surfaced clearly in the SE demo and Console UI. This sprint produced a viable prototype plan; next step is an internal spike and a small customer pilot with one retail and one finserv account.

Unresolved items that need engineering estimates: kernel conversion layer feasibility, memory cost of hybrid cache, end-to-end audit pipeline for fallback events.

References / attachments: links above + internal slide deck (attached in SE drive folder).
